problem: VLN agents rely on whole-image RGB features and heavy offline data augmentation (extra environments, more parameters/data); the distinct roles of foreground (semantic cues) and background (spatial connectivity) in observations remain unexplored.
motivation: Foreground objects matter when locating targets (e.g., the mug) while background layout matters when traversing (e.g., the corridor). Exploiting this intrinsic diversity could improve generalization to unseen environments without extra environments or architecture changes.
key_idea: Disentangle each viewpoint into foreground and background CLIP features via landmark-guided segmentation, then use two-stage consensus voting (multi-agent, multi-trajectory) to choose the best feature among original, foreground and background per viewpoint as online augmentation.
insight: Disentangled features help even when replacing originals directly: CLIP-original gives SR 48.14 vs FG 54.44 and BG 53.14 on REVERIE val-unseen, so the gain is not from the CLIP encoder. Random (stochastic) selection degrades results (BG 49.05 SR vs 53.14 direct replacement), while voting-based selection gives the best SR/SPL (54.62/38.17). Voting statistics show REVERIE prefers foreground, while R2R prefers background.
method: Semantic-enhanced landmark identification: RAM++ detects objects; Qwen2.5-VL names room type and 7-8 key objects per panorama; all-MiniLM-L6-v2 similarity filters detections to key landmarks.

Spatially-disentangled feature extraction: EVF-SAM produces text-driven landmark masks for the 36 views of each viewpoint; the mask (FG) and its complement (BG) are applied to the images and encoded by CLIP-ViT-B/16 into I^fg and I^bg.

Multi-agent voting: three frozen agents, each pretrained on one feature type (ori/fg/bg), run on the training split; the score is the cross-entropy of action logits vs ground truth; the lowest-score feature is chosen per viewpoint per trajectory.
Multi-trajectory voting: majority vote across all training trajectories containing the viewpoint gives a final feature label per viewpoint.
Viewpoint-level feature augmentation: the selected feature (ori/fg/bg) replaces the viewpoint feature in a DUET pipeline with no architecture change and negligible extra training cost.
Stochastic augmentation (comparison): picks the augmented feature with probability 0.5 per viewpoint.

setting.backbone: DUET (trained; features from CLIP-ViT-B/16 with RAM++, Qwen2.5-VL, MiniLM, EVF-SAM as frozen preprocessors)
setting.training_data: REVERIE / R2R training splits; pretraining with MLM, SAP, OG for 100k iterations (batch 32), fine-tuning 20k iterations (batch 12); no extra environments
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views per viewpoint) with disentangled foreground/background CLIP features
setting.privileged: none at test time (voting labels are precomputed on training split using GT action labels)

numbers.extra: online consensus augmentation; multi-agent voting uses three pretrained agents

results: COFA reaches REVERIE val-unseen SR 54.62 / SPL 38.17 / RGS 36.07, above the DUET baseline (46.98/33.73/32.15) and the offline-augmentation RAM (51.89/35.00/34.31). On R2R it gets val-unseen SR 74.2 / SPL 64.2 / NE 2.92 and test-unseen SR 74.7 / SPL 62.6 / NE 2.86, versus the DUET baseline at 71 / 61 / 3.30 (val-unseen).
limitations: Voting trades off object grounding: RGS/RGSPL are slightly lower than direct FG replacement (36.07 vs 36.59 RGS).
Relies on a heavy stack of off-the-shelf models (RAM++, Qwen2.5-VL, EVF-SAM, CLIP) for preprocessing, and on three separately pretrained agents for voting.
Validated only on DUET with discrete R2R/REVERIE; the paper claims but does not show generality to other VLN methods.
